Abingdon School in Partnership
Abingdon Science Partnership
The Abingdon Science Partnership (ASP) works with community and national organisations and all sectors of education to support high quality STEM learning and experiences for all.
The ASP is a main supporter of the annual Abingdon ATOM Festival of Science and Technology; administers lead school status for the Institute of Physics; coordinates the Abingdon Partnership of Schools; and leads Saturday Science Clubs on behalf of Science Oxford. The ASP has developed a regular programme of STEM workshops and long-term investigation activities to enhance STEM learning in local primary schools. A-level and GCSE extension workshops and research projects with academic partners are a key feature of ASP’s work with other secondary schools, as well as offering classes in GCSE Astronomy and other enrichment opportunities, such as being a Student Ambassador for the ATOM Festival.
A range of online resources for all ages can also be found here.

Subjects
Computer Science
Computer Science is compulsory from First to Third Year. The GCSE course looks in more detail at the discipline of Computer Science and focuses on students’ Python programming skills. The A Level takes the study of the elements of the academic discipline further, for example looking more formally at algorithms and data structures, and learning object oriented and functional programming.
Further information about the Computer Science Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

Drama
The aim of the Drama Department is to instil in our students a life-long enjoyment of drama. We are incredibly fortunate to have two drama studios, a dedicated technical team and use of the Amey Theatre for productions. Throughout the First and Second Years, students are taught key principles including physical theatre, improvisation, and significant genres helping them to develop essential transferable skills such as collaboration and creative thinking. Students can opt to study for GCSE and A Level, engaging with practitioners like Stanislavski and rehearsing scripted texts.
Further information about the Drama Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

Subjects
Ancient History
Ancient History is taught as part of the Classics course up to Third Year and as a standalone subject for GCSE and A Level. Developing the ability to evaluate ancient sources (all studied in English), classes consider the agendas of those who wrote them and how that affects their reliability for what they tell us. Whilst considering in detail world-changing historical moments that are compelling in their own right, the courses also strongly encourage reflection on how study of the ancient world offers insight and comment on contemporary events.
We run an extensive range of trips beyond the classroom, as we feel that live performances of ancient drama and surviving archaeological remains offer unique opportunities to access the ancient world.
Further information about the Classics Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

Subjects
Art and Design
The Art Department is a thriving hub of creativity. We aim to develop ambitious and imaginative work through a wide range of approaches – from painting and screen printing to ceramic sculpture and digital drawing – each informed by historical and contemporary art practice. In order that their work should have a context, pupils are helped to relate their work to other artists through regular gallery visits and the resources of the departmental library.
Our exceptional facilities include four large classrooms, a ceramics room, a dark room, and a large Sixth Form studio. Many of our students go on to study at top universities for careers in fine art, film and architecture.
Further information about the Art Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

An Introduction to Abingdon

Subjects
Biology
Compulsory to GCSE and optional at A Level, Biology at Abingdon is taught across six teaching laboratories. The Lower School and Third Year courses aim to give an introduction to various topics and key concepts that will ultimately be covered in more detail in the GCSE course as well as trying to develop some of the core skills needed for the subject. Topics range all the way from biological molecules up to ecological/environmental topics. While factual knowledge is key, we emphasise applying knowledge in unfamiliar situations and mastering practical, experimental skills. Outside normal lessons, subject clinics, Sixth Form extension classes and sessions for aspiring medics are offered, complemented by trips and a number of Other Half activities.
Further information about the Biology Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

Chemistry
Compulsory to GCSE and optional at A Level, we secure a firm appreciation of the fundamentals of chemical structures, methodology and reactivity in the First to Third Years, inspiring our pupils through practical chemistry and critical thought. We follow the Edexcel at both IGCSE and A Level, where we take students beyond the confines of exam specifications so they can confidently take their study of the subject to the next levels and appreciate the broader applications of the subject within modern day life.

Subjects
English
At the heart of the school curriculum, English is a compulsory subject to GCSE. Our curriculum is rigorous and challenging, aiming to foster a love of literature and develop excellent communication and critical thinking skills. In the First and Second Years, we foster a love of literature while developing reading and writing skills through drama, poetry and prose fiction and non-fiction texts. Third Year opens with the study of a classic novel, which is used to develop pupils’ critical thinking skills while offering a stimulus for writing tasks, followed by a range of units designed to embed the core skills required at IGCSE. In the Fourth and Fifth Years we follow the Edexcel IGCSE courses. Students who choose the English Literature A Level (OCR) study Renaissance drama and poetry and American literature for their exams, while pursuing coursework tasks on a selection of post-1900 works.
Further information about the English Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

Geography
Geography is a compulsory subject up to the end of Third Year, then optional for GCSE and A Level. It is a social science that complements a wide range of subjects, providing an excellent basis for a contemporary education and widening career opportunities through integral research, analysis and communication skills.
We aim to instil a spirit of inquiry and encourage pupils to be curious about the world, thinking analytically and critically about both human and physical geography and current global issues.
The department features one of the country’s first dedicated GIS suites (Geographic Information System) and we have a dedicated support co-ordinator to help deliver our ambitious programme. Regular field excursions are integral, including overseas trips for Sixth Form and Middle School to destinations like Iceland and the Azores.
Further information about the Geography Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

ABINGDON SCHOOL IN PARTNERSHIP COMMUNITY COLLABORATION CHALLENGE
DIRECTOR OF PARTNERSHIPS At Abingdon, our Partnership work is embedded in all areas of school life. As a school we look to play a positive role in the wider community and collaborate with schools locally for mutual benefit. Students and staff are encouraged to challenge themselves through participation in Partnerships. Central to an Abingdon School education is our nationally respected Partnership programme where community, collaboration and challenge run through all aspects of school life. To help our students become ambitious and resilient, staff to be collaborative and reflective, parents to feel informed and engaged, and for all stakeholders to feel supported by, and given opportunities through, Partnerships. Students are trained in empathetic listening, creative loitering and mental health awareness to provide invaluable support. Students are also able to signpost students to helpful resources or further support. Throughout the year students take part in challenge days and joint events. Challenge days are often supported by local business partners and bring students together to collaborate and develop new skills. The Business Language challenge is an opportunity for linguists to work together on a marketing challenge in their chosen language. They develop a product and market it to suppliers taking part in real life scenarios. The Faraday Challenge sees students compete on an engineering task and use their design skills to solve a real life problem. Other events include Robocon, a computer science challenge, the Naboj Maths Challenge and various Model United Nations events. These events bring teams of students together from across Abingdon and the surrounding ares and students relish the opportunity to meet new people. Subjects
Business
Offered at A Level, Business is a dynamic subject in which students learn about the diverse nature of business enterprise and the interdependence of the various parts of the business world. Students explore business success and business failure, investigate local, national and global business markets, and understand how businesses need to adapt and respond strategically to the changing environment in which they operate to survive and grow. This constant evolutionary process makes business a fascinating subject.
Extension activities include writing for the School magazine, participating in the investment and trading club, and hearing from guest entrepreneurs.
We recommend students pursue only one of Business or Economics to full A Level due to perceived content overlap.
Further information about the Business Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

Subjects
Economics
Economics is offered at A Level only at Abingdon. As economics relates to every aspect of life, from the decisions we make as individuals or families, to the structures created by governments and firms, it is an extremely relevant subject. Students are encouraged to go beyond the passive acceptance of ‘the facts’ and to grapple with the subtleties, complexities and value judgments implicit in Economics, and we seek to foster a spirit of inquiry that gives them the capacity to make critical judgments. Extension activities include writing for the School magazine, participating in the investment and trading club, and entering national essay competitions.
We recommend students pursue only one of Economics or Business to full A Level due to content overlap.
Further information about the Economics Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

Subjects
Electronics
Studying Electronics gives students the opportunity to learn a subject rarely taught in schools and one that stands out on a CV. Former Abingdon students who have gone on to study Engineering report that GCSE Electronics provided a strong foundation for their first year at university, and it also offers an excellent basis for studying Computing at A Level. The course is taught through a hands-on, practical approach, with each student provided with their own breadboard, power supply and components to develop skills both in school and at home. This engaging method is popular with students and is reflected in our excellent results.
Further information about the Electronics Department curriculum can be found in the curriculum documents available for download on the main curriculum page.

About
Senior Leadership Team
The Governors of Abingdon delegate leadership of the School to the Head and the Senior Leadership Team. The Leadership Team is responsible for the day to day running of the School and for delivering Abingdon’s development plan. Members of the Leadership Team have specific responsibilities within the overall management of the School: Academic, Pastoral Care, External Relations, Educational Development and Finance and Operations.
The Senior Leadership Team:
Jossie Austen - Director of External Relations
Jossie joined Abingdon from Witham Hall School where she was the Director of External Relations. She has worked with a broad range of senior and prep school clients in the Independent Schools Sector as a freelance consultant for the Philanthropy Team at RSAcademics and has previously held positions responsible for Marketing, Admissions and Development at Ludgrove and Summer Fields, where she also ran a boarding house for five years. Jossie hails from New York, moving to the UK to read History of Art at the University of St Andrews followed by an MA in Art Business at Sotheby’s Institute of Art, London. Prior to her transition to education, Jossie worked in the Arts for collections including Oxford University Museums & Gardens, MoMA New York and the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice.
Jossie joined Abingdon as Director of External Relations in 2024. She holds Foundation-wide responsibility for Admissions, Alumni Relations, Communications, Development, Marketing and Partnerships. Together these key operations provide cohesion and a sense of belonging for all stakeholders across the greater Abingdon Foundation community. Having worked in pastoral and administrative roles within schools for nearly two decades, she is passionate about the role of an independent school education in transforming lives.
Nicky Black - Head of Abingdon Prep School
After graduating from the University of Durham with a degree in Education, Nicky went on to teach and lead in a number of top Prep Schools in various roles, including Head of Maths, Head of Pre-Prep, Director of Studies, and Deputy Head. In recent years, Nicky was Head at Dulwich College Kindergarten and Infants School before relocating to Oxfordshire to become Head of Cokethorpe Prep School.
While passionate about education, she is also a strong advocate for the outdoors. Nicky loves nothing more than being in the mountains, whether that’s hiking in the summer or skiing in the winter. As a mother of two teenagers, she knows how important family life is and how crucial it is to find a school that feels right for you as parents and where your child will be happy and truly flourish.
Justin Hodges - Director of Finance and Operations
Prior to Abingdon Justin was at Vodafone for 12 years where he held various positions, including Head of Financial Planning & Analysis at Vodafone UK, Southern Europe Financial Controller for Vodafone Group, Head of Strategy at Vodafone Italy and Director of Vodafone Ventures. Prior to this, he worked for Goldman Sachs investment bank in London and San Francisco. Justin graduated from Oxford University with a MEng in Engineering, Economics & Management, and a MSc in Management Studies. Justin is also an OA.
Justin became the Director of Finance & Operations in 2015. His responsibilities are Foundation-wide and include finance, facilities development and maintenance, compliance, security, IT and Information Systems, health and safety, grounds, gardens, catering, housekeeping, financial assistance programmes, company secretary as well as commercial activities in Abingdon School Enterprises.
Helen Keevil - Deputy Head (Pastoral) & Designated Safeguarding Lead
An Exeter graduate in Modern Foreign Languages, Helen’s love of, and passion for, languages translates to teaching classes of 11 to 18 year olds across all abilities. A product of a co-educational upbringing, she joined Abingdon from Epsom College where she was instrumental in introducing girls at junior level in a day and boarding environment. Her roles included boarding Housemistress; Head of Year monitoring academic progress for the GCSE cohort; Head of PSHE; and EDI and Mental Health Lead. Helen is particularly interested in digital wellbeing. She coaches hockey, football and tennis, and is a keen runner. As part of her role as pastoral lead on SLT, she trained senior student digital mentors, peer mentors of various ages and delivered regular training to teachers, gap students, parents and matrons on pastoral issues, safeguarding and e-safety updates. She tutors for the Boarding Schools Association, sits on the steering group for EDI policy and Gender Agenda initiatives for the Royal National Children’s Springboard Foundation, is a member of the advisory board of the Votes For Schools debating platform and enjoys raising awareness of positive mental health issues through local charity work.
Helen’s responsibilities include the oversight of the welfare of all pupils, leading pastoral systems through Heads of House, section heads and tutors, plus the counselling team and health centre. She is the Designated Safeguarding Lead and oversees the boarding and day structures across houses as well pupil induction. She has a key role in implementing the transition to welcoming girls to Abingdon in 2026 heading up the pastoral workstream. She is the school’s Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Lead and line manages the Heads of House, the Head of Wellbeing and Mental Health, the Chaplain and the Senior Nurse. She also oversees all rewards, sanctions and discipline issues, whilst coaching sport and teaching MFL.
Graeme May - Senior Deputy Head
Having read English at Oxford, Graeme began his teaching career at Pocklington School and, after short stints at Blundell’s and Lord Wandsworth College, moved to St Paul’s School in London where he was at various times Head of Drama, Deputy Head of English and a teacher of Latin alongside his English. Whilst he was at St Paul’s he undertook a two-year teacher exchange with Sydney Grammar School, Australia. On return to London, Graeme was quickly off to a Head of English post at Cheltenham College, where he also started up curricular drama, was editor of a number of school publications and visiting tutor to a boarding house before moving on to Abingdon after 5 years. He inspects regularly for ISI.
Having served as Deputy Head (Academic) since 2007, Graeme was appointed Senior Deputy Head in 2023. He is responsible for the day-to-day organisation of the school, has general oversight of the Other Half, takes a leading role in pupil recruitment and deputises for the Head in his absence. Throughout his time at Abingdon, Graeme has taught his core subject of English, in addition to Drama, Ancient History, Computing and PSHCE. He continues to direct drama productions when he can.
Ben Whitworth - Acting Deputy Head (Academic)
Ben has been at Abingdon School since 2010 and has been involved in all aspects of school life. He studied Natural Sciences at Magdalene College, Cambridge and, after a brief stint in IT, trained as a teacher in London. Before becoming Acting Deputy Head (Academic), Ben has been the Director of eLearning and Head of Biology.
Ben’s core role is the strategic management of all academic aspects of the school. This includes an overview of the curriculum and the leadership of the Heads of Department. Ben has always enjoyed providing opportunities for students through the Other Half programme including coaching rowing to Third Year and, as part of the Sixth Form team, has helped support students applying to read Medicine, Veterinary Science and Dentistry.

Inspection Reports
April 2026 School Inspection Report
In April 2026, the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) carried out a School Inspection at Abingdon School.
The School Inspection reports on standards relating to: leadership and management, and governance; quality of education, training and recreation; pupils’ physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing; pupils’ social and economic education and contribution to society; and safeguarding. Judgments within the report are given either as ‘met’ or as ‘not met’.
We are delighted to report that standards at Abingdon School were met in all five categories.
Abingdon School ISI School Inspection Report 2026
“Pupils engage appropriately and contribute to discussion, articulating their ideas and applying their learning in more complex and independent ways.”
